clue.text: Fiddle by accountant name of Sharp

blocks.note: a rebec is a medieval stringed instrument played with a bow, an early fiddle
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Some financial fiddle cooked up by an accountant on behalf of a client called Sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' reads as fraud alongside 'accountant', but it is the old instrument. Becky Sharp is the heroine of Thackeray's Vanity Fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Becky Sharp, the scheming heroine of Thackeray's novel Vanity Fair, bears this as her full first name.

clue.text: Queen has sway over cruel King

blocks.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
IC is short for 'in charge', which is having sway over something
hard as in harsh or unfeeling

explanation.surface: A queen dominates a cruel monarch at court.
explanation.walkthrough: IC stands for 'in charge', a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English monarchs carried this name, among them the Lionheart and the Third, so it names a king.

clue.text: One cannot see the point of this

definitions.text: One cannot see the point of this

blocks.clueFragment: One cannot see the point of this
blocks.note: surface reading: something so pointless that nobody grasps its purpose
setter's reading: literally, wearing this you cannot see, as in pinning the tail on the donkey

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannot see the point' sounds like bafflement; it is meant literally, of someone whose eyes are covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth tied over the eyes stops the wearer seeing anything at all, including where to aim.

clue.text: Plutocracy nicely absorbs such as Diogenes

indicators.note: the phrase soaks up the solution inside its own letters, so look within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Rule by the rich comfortably takes in a philosopher who scorned wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes of Sinope was the most famous member of the Cynic school of Greek philosophy, which shunned convention.

clue.text: Recorder takes chair - five sit out

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed from its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recorder of a meeting takes the chair while five members sit it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests a musical instrument or a judge; here it is a keeper of records.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist keeps and catalogues historical documents and records, so is a recorder in that sense.

clue.text: What colour? Sleep on it!

blocks.note: first meaning: a pale yellowish-brown shade
second meaning: a square mattress section once issued to soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep on it!' sounds like advice to postpone a decision; it means a thing you lie on. Army beds were once made up of three square cushions known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a light brown shade used for pottery and fabric and an old military mattress square.

clue.text: Staff in-sporting take-over bid

blocks.note: surface reading: employees inside a sports company launch a bid to buy it
setter's reading: a short staff that one runner hands over to the next in a relay race

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphens push 'take-over' toward a corporate buyout; it is the changeover in a relay, where a stick is passed between runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay runner carries a short stick, which is a staff, and must pass it to a teammate at each changeover.

clue.text: Little to report when these are used

definitions.text: Little to report when these are used

blocks.clueFragment: Little to report when these are used
blocks.note: surface reading: some measures that leave journalists with no news
setter's reading: a report is the bang of a gun, which these devices muffle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' reads as a news story; a report is also the loud crack of a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices fitted to a gun barrel to muffle the noise of firing leave only a little sound, a quiet report.

clue.text: Prompted to produce a rude note

indicators.note: to produce something is to make it up anew, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
G is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Someone was egged on to write an offensive message.
explanation.definitionFit: Urged and prompted are synonyms, both meaning encouraged or pushed someone to act.

clue.text: Theatre conversion on that account not much used now

definitions.text: on that account not much used now

indicators.note: a conversion changes a building into a new shape, so these letters are remodelled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre turned into flats is rarely used for shows any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not much used now' flags an archaic word, fittingly old-fashioned beside an old theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adverb meant 'for that reason' or 'on account of that', and now survives mainly in older texts.

clue.text: Speaking of money a point of view

indicators.note: speaking means saying the next word out loud, so its sound matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: a coin is a piece of money

explanation.surface: Like a chat about finance offering a particular perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: The word survives mainly in Shakespeare's phrase 'coign of vantage', a good spot from which to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A coign is a projecting corner of a building, and a coign of vantage is a favourable viewpoint for observing.

clue.text: Register a cute goal after a scuffle

indicators.note: a scuffle is a confused tussle, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A referee records a neat goal scored following a goalmouth scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a systematic list of items, which is what a register also is.

clue.text: Devotion to the Christian era so to speak

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the Christian era in dates
diction is the manner of speaking, how one enunciates

explanation.surface: Devotion to the faith since Christ's time, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' looks like a throwaway aside but supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dedication to something, and devotion can mean the same strong attachment.

clue.text: Dig in region Eve came from

definitions.text: Dig in region Eve came from

blocks.clueFragment: Dig in region Eve came from
blocks.note: surface reading: an archaeological excavation in the Garden of Eden
setter's reading: Eve was made from Adam's rib, so this is a dig in the ribs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' and 'region' point to archaeology in Eden; Genesis says Eve was made from Adam's rib, giving a dig in the ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle poke in someone's ribs with the elbow, to get their attention, is exactly this action.

clue.text: Dead Sea rubbish

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on family trees
the Ross Sea is an inlet of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica

explanation.surface: Junk floating in the Dead Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead Sea' looks like one place name; split it, and the sea is a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is the scum skimmed from molten metal, and by extension any worthless waste matter.

clue.text: Three pips a second - not always

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the two words some times

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: a handful of time signals within one second, a few times
second meaning: on occasion, now and then

explanation.walkthrough: The pips are the short beeps of the BBC radio time signal, each one marking a time; several of them are some times.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done now and then, on certain occasions only, happens on some occasions but not always.

clue.text: Tool to finish the job

blocks.note: first meaning: an instrument or utensil
second meaning: to carry out or put into effect

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction about needing a tool; the noun and the verb are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is a utensil or device; as a verb it means to put a plan into effect fully.

clue.text: Dancers take turns demonstrating this

blocks.note: surface reading: dancers show something one after another, waiting their turn
setter's reading: the dancers literally spin round, performing turns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take turns' suggests a rota; in ballet a turn is a spin on one foot.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet this is a complete spin of the body on the point of one foot, a classic turn.

clue.text: “Soap and — . . . more deadly in the long run.” (Mark Twain)

definitions.text: “Soap and — . . . more deadly in the long run.” (Mark Twain)

blocks.clueFragment: “Soap and — . . . more deadly in the long run.”
blocks.note: surface reading: a quotation with a gap, as if soap had a deadly partner
setter's reading: Twain's full line says soap and the missing word are less sudden than a massacre but deadlier over time

explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the solver supplies the word Twain paired with soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain's quip is that washing and schooling are slower than a massacre but more deadly over time, so schooling fills the gap.

clue.text: Measure of Shanks's Pony

blocks.note: surface reading: the height of some horse owned by a man named Shanks
setter's reading: shanks's pony is British slang for going on foot, so a device that measures walking

explanation.walkthrough: Shanks's pony is a British idiom meaning your own legs, that is walking; it looks like a real horse.
explanation.definitionFit: This device counts a walker's steps to estimate the distance travelled on foot.

clue.text: Horseman's choice of entrance announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the sound of the phrase counts rather than its spelling

blocks.note: choosing an entrance is picking a door

explanation.surface: A rider at a gameshow is told which door to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bullfight this mounted man goads the bull with a lance, so he is a horseman of the ring.

clue.text: Small change by a composer

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is set beside the other

blocks.note: sous were low-value old French coins, a byword for small change
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer made a minor revision to a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small change' reads as a minor alteration; it is loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the American bandmaster who wrote marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Where arms are put aside say

definitions.text: Where arms are put aside say

blocks.clueFragment: Where arms are put aside say
blocks.note: surface reading: a place of disarmament, where weapons are laid down
setter's reading: put aside means stored away for later use, as weapons are kept in a store

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put aside' suggests giving up arms; it means stockpiling them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a building or store where weapons and ammunition are kept ready for use.

clue.text: Tobacco Company is out to make explorer return

indicators.note: something that is out is excluded, so those letters are dropped
to return is to go back the way you came, so what remains is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A tobacco firm is on strike, forcing a traveller to come home.
explanation.walkthrough: TOBACCO without CO leaves TOBAC.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Venetian navigator who sailed for England and reached North America in 1497.

clue.text: Signal to the first scout to take shelter

indicators.note: one part taking another means it holds it inside itself

blocks.note: Baden-Powell, founder of the Scout movement, is known by his initials
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A scout leader is sent a warning to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Baden-Powell founded the Boy Scouts, making him the original scout.
explanation.definitionFit: A short high-pitched electronic sound used as an alert is a signal.

clue.text: Sad informer found in Kentucky

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A miserable police informant turns up in Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for someone who informs on criminals to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky is nicknamed the Bluegrass State after the meadow grass that grows there, and the country music style comes from the region.

clue.text: Agent loses right without money

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a broker acts as an agent buying and selling for others
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An agent loses a legal entitlement and is left penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone short of cash, out of funds and unable to pay their bills, is in this state.

clue.text: Understand note on file

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another sits above it

blocks.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
a rasp is a coarse file for wood or metal

explanation.surface: Make sense of a memo kept in a folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' and 'file' suggest office paperwork; they are a musical note and a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to comprehend it fully, a common figurative synonym of understand.

clue.text: Think of a gondola, perhaps, for one's heart-throb

blocks.note: to dream of something is to think of it longingly
a gondola is an example of a boat, as 'perhaps' signals

explanation.surface: Imagine a Venetian gondola ride with someone you adore.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is an informal word for a very attractive person, someone you idolise romantically.

clue.text: A right outsider

blocks.note: taken as written
a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A genuine underdog, the sort with little chance of winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A right outsider' sounds like a total stranger, using 'right' as an intensifier; it is a legal right.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or stranger who does not belong, which is what an outsider is.

clue.text: Posterior? Answer back possibly or not at all

indicators.note: possibly means in some other possible form, so the letters may be rearranged
not at all means that word is wholly absent, so its letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shows their backside: is that a cheeky reply or nothing at all?
explanation.walkthrough: POSTERIOR without its closing OR leaves POSTERI to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, so it is to answer back; in fencing it is a counter-thrust.

clue.text: Enrol for space unit plane manoeuvre

indicators.note: a manoeuvre is a deliberate movement, so the letters shift into a new position

blocks.note: an em is a printer's unit of space, the width of the letter M
the letters of plane, rearranged

explanation.surface: Sign up for a space mission involving aircraft manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space unit' hints at astronauts; it is a printing measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To empanel is to enter names on a list, especially a jury list, so it means to enrol.
